by.description: The participant that disconnected this client. Absent when the request named nobody.

restart.description: The restart the shutdown-daemon requester sent: true when a replacement daemon follows, false when the session stops. Sent only to a client that negotiated daemon-shutdown-restart-v1 in set-client-info, and absent when the requester did not say (session.shutdown, an older CLI).

view.description: Relay sub-view name; exactly one of lease or view.

scope.description: "view" when only the client's own view was detached; the connection stays.

restore_progress.description: Answered while the owner restores its session too, at once, with lifecycle_ready false, placeholder session fields (registry_id and generation empty, revisions 0) and restore. Without it a restoring owner holds the request until the restore ends. A ready owner ignores it.

revisions.description: Adds api_revision, min_api_revision, api_version, min_api_version, crate_version, install and update_command to the reply. Off by default so strict older SDK decoders keep reading the reply.

after.description: With limit: skip this many workspaces in sidebar order first (the next of the page before). Ignored without limit.

known.description: The identity and revisions of the whole tree the client holds ({} when none). When all are current the result is unchanged: true with empty workspaces; keep the tree you hold. Otherwise the whole tree with its tree_revision.

limit.description: Only the first limit workspaces in sidebar order, with total, and at most 64 KiB of rows (at least one row). A reply with fewer than total workspaces has no tree_revision.

since.description: The cursor of the last reply the client applied. When the daemon still holds every change past it, the result is delta: true with only the changed workspace entries (changed, keyed by id) and the ids that went away (removed); otherwise the whole tree. Both carry the epoch and seq to send next. Takes precedence over known, limit and after.

view.description: Relay sub-view of this connection; omitted marks the caller's own view.

Relay sub-view name, 1-128 printable characters; exactly one of lease or view.

restore_progress.description: While the owner restores its session: refused at once with error_code server.restoring and error_details {lifecycle_ready: false, restore}, instead of held until the restore ends. A ready owner ignores it.

api_revision.description: The API revision the client reads and writes. An older revision within the daemon's range is translated both ways by the daemon; a newer client translates for itself; an older one than min_api_revision is refused. Absent: revision 12.

api_version.description: A dated API version, YYYY-MM-DD (for example 2026-11-24). The daemon serves the newest revision dated on or before it and answers with api_version and api_revision; a date before min_api_version is refused; with api_revision too, both must name the same revision. Absent: unchanged behaviour. Promise: cmux-tui/spec/api-versioning.md.

acpmux.AnswerMeta.description:
`_meta.acpmux` on an answer. Every field is optional; a relayed allow
carries the decision proof, the person's app may say whose answer it
relays, and a peer forwarding for its Web client says `via: "web"`.

answeredBy.description: `{device, feedItem}`, from the person's connection only.

approverDecision.description:
An enrolled approver's signed answer beside `decisionNonce`: a phone's
(`hub/approvers.rs`) or a Mac's (`hub/mac_approvers.rs`).

approverDecisions.description:
A group's one-time allow from an enrolled Mac (`_acpmux/permission_group_respond`):
one signed allow per pending member of the group, by permission id.

acpmux.ApprovedPlan.description:
The plan the person last approved in a chat (`hub/plan_build.rs` `approved_plan`): Claude
Code's ExitPlanMode, or a Grok, Cursor or Gemini plan approval, answered with an allow. The
pane keeps it in sight while the agent builds it (Leo's feature map, 2026-11-23: "plan pane
that stays during the build"); a newer approval replaces it.

at.description: When it was approved, Unix ms.

edited.description: The person edited the plan before approving it.

markdown.description: The plan as approved, Markdown: the person's edit when they made one.

turn.description: The chat's turn count when it was approved.

acpmux.ApproverDecision.description:
`{approver, expiresAt, signature}`: ECDSA P-256 / SHA-256, raw `r || s` as
lowercase hex, over the approver's message for this exact answer.

afterSeq.description: Page forward from here (oldest first) when `beforeSeq` is absent.

attending.description:
False attaches showing the chat to a person who is away (`_acpmux/view` `attending`): it
sees nothing, so a reconnect while they are away keeps the chat's unread; default true.

beforeSeq.description: The newest `limit` records before this one.

eventStream.description:
Send every matching record as `_acpmux/event`; else the agent's
updates arrive as ACP `session/update` and acpmux's own as
`_acpmux/event`.

hold.description:
The hold of a chat whose rows come from the row store (`attach-hold-v1`,
`server/requests.rs` `hold_attach_filter`): no page and no log read, only the exact
page-state `kinds` streamed live; needs `eventStream: true`.

omitTimeBreakdown.description:
True from a client that never draws the breakdown (the phone): the reply's `session`
leaves `timeBreakdown` out whatever its version (`server/requests/time_breakdown_gate.rs`).

quietHidden.description:
True: the client draws nothing of the chat while it is hidden (`visible: false`), so the
agent's `session/update` stream is left out until `_acpmux/view` shows it, which then sends
one `_acpmux/lagged` naming the chat (`server/view.rs`); default false.

settled.description:
Answer from the chat's settled view first (`settled-attach-v1`,
`server/requests/settled_attach.rs`): a read, falling back to a plain page.

timeBreakdownVersion.description:
The `timeBreakdownVersion` of the breakdown copy this client holds (from an earlier
attach): while the chat's copy is the same, the reply's `session` leaves `timeBreakdown`
out (`server/requests/time_breakdown_gate.rs`). Absent, or another version: sent whole.

visible.description: False attaches without showing the chat (`hub/seen.rs`); default true.

waitLogs.description: Wait for restart-time log restoration before answering; false serves the page immediately.

hasMore.description: More records lie beyond this page.

pageThrough.description:
How far the page holds: every record of the kinds asked from the page's first one up to it
is in the page (a peer's copy of the chat, `hub/peer_snapshot.rs`, covers that far). The
log's last seq, read before the page, for the newest page; a page of older records
(`beforeSeq`) or a forward one with more to read holds only to its own last record.

presence.description: Who has the chat open now, this attachment included (`hub/presence.rs`).

readThrough.description:
The attaching person's seen cursor (`hub/seen.rs` `read_through`): the newest log seq they
saw while attending; null before they saw any. An older acpmux leaves it out.

timeBreakdownVersion.description:
The version of the session's `timeBreakdown` copy (a hash of it); null when it has none.
Sent back as the attach's `timeBreakdownVersion`, the next reply leaves an unchanged copy
out of `session`. An older acpmux leaves it out.

turnOpener.description:
The prompt that opened the turn the page starts inside, when the page starts inside one
with older records before it (`server/requests/turn_opener.rs`); null otherwise. An older
acpmux leaves it out, and its client reads it with `_acpmux/events`.

acpmux.Author.description:
The person a request comes from (`hub/author.rs`): stamped by the daemon that admitted
them, and accepted only from the unix socket or a peer forwarding for its own.

approval.description: A link guest's prompts wait for the chat owner's approval.

id.description: `tailnet:<login>` until accounts are mapped, then `user_…`; one line of at most 256 bytes.

acpmux.AuthorMetaFields.description: `_meta.acpmux` of a request that may name its person; other fields pass.

acpmux.Autocompact.description: Whether a harness's autocompact is capped (`UsageStats.autocompact`).

oneOf.description: A flag, env or setting caps it.
Nothing caps it: the harness's own default applies.
Not known: its argv is not this daemon's, or a value or file it reads could not be read.

acpmux.CapacityWait.description:
A chat waiting for capacity (`hub/capacity_wait.rs`): a turn cut by an overloaded model, an
exhausted account pool or the account's rate limit, which acpmux continues by itself. A
client draws it as one calm state ("Waiting for capacity, about 40 s"; in a list "paused for
capacity, resumes ~22:41"), never as a failed turn, and keeps `error` for a details
disclosure.

error.description: The harness's raw error, cut to 600 characters, for a details disclosure only.

resumesAt.description: When it goes on (epoch ms); absent while the continuation is still being decided.

since.description: Since when it waits (epoch ms): the cut turn's end.

turnId.description: The cut turn the wait continues, when there is one.

acpmux.ChunkDelta.description:
`_acpmux/chunk` (`chunk-deltas-v1`, `server/chunk_deltas.rs`): an `agent_message_chunk`
record, to a client whose `initialize` sent `_meta.acpmux.chunkDeltas: true`, as a delta of the
last `_acpmux/event` it got that carried this `chunkRef`. The event it stands for is that one's
params with this `seq`, `at` that frame's plus `dt` (the previous `_acpmux/chunk` of the same
`ref` counts as that frame), and `msg.params.update.content.text` this `text`. A `ref` the
client does not hold: it reads again from its cursor (`_acpmux/attach {afterSeq}`).

dt.description: Unix ms since the frame before it of this `ref`.

facts.description: In footer order (`FactKind::ALL`); a fact with nothing to say is left out.

items.description: Worst level first, then the oldest `since` (an unknown one last).

acpmux.CreatedBy.description:
Who created a session (`hub/created_by.rs`), the shape cmux-tui's
`workspace.create {created_by}` takes.

session.description: The acpmux session whose agent created it; only for `agent`.

workspace.description:
The cmux workspace it was created from (lowercase UUID): the agent session's
workspace for an agent, else the one the create named.

oneOf.description: This host's app, or a connection that proved it is the person.

An agent session: its shell's `acpmux new` (a proven caller token) or its
`start_session` tool.
Any other client: a script or the CLI outside a chat.

acpmux.Enforcement.description: What limits the session's agent as far as acpmux can tell.

policy.description:
The acpmux permission policy (the session's own, else the daemon
default), or `unknown`.

acpmux.ErrorDetails.description: The facts of a typed failure (`errorKind`); only the keys that apply are present.

binary.description: The program that could not start.

path.description: The folder whose disk is full or low.

peer.description: The peer, by its name in `acpmux host ls`.

queued.description: The message is held in the durable outbox and goes when the peer or daemon is back.

acpmux.EventKinds.description:
Which records a page or an event stream carries: one kind, or any of
several. Absent or null: every record.

afterSeq.description: Records after this one; it may not lie beyond the last record.

beforeSeq.description: The newest `limit` records before this one.

inOrder.description:
True: answered in order, after every line already queued to this connection, as an attach
is. A pane's stall check sets it: it compares the newest record with what the stream has
delivered, so an answer ahead of the records queued before it reads a healthy stream as
stalled (`server/outbound.rs` `reply_lane`). Default false: a tool call's read goes ahead.

promptIndex.description:
The prompts before `beforeSeq`, newest page first and oldest first within a page, each cut
to its id and the start of its text (`Hub::prompt_index`). `limit` and `maxBytes` bound the
page; `hasMore` says an older page remains, whose `beforeSeq` is the first event's seq.

sinceSeen.description:
Read the transcript after this reader's New line, or their persisted readThrough cursor while away.
Without a cursor the page is empty. Incompatible with afterSeq, beforeSeq, promptIndex and turnOpener.

subagent.description:
Only this subagent's own records: the updates acpmux tagged with it and those that start
or change it (`EventFilter::of_subagent`). A subagent pane reads its subagent with it.

createdAt.description:
The session the page is of (its `createdAt`): a session recreated under the same id while
the page was asked is another journal (`hub/peer_snapshot.rs`).

pageThrough.description:
How far the page holds: every record of the kinds asked after `afterSeq` up to it is in the
page (`hub/peer_snapshot.rs`). The log's last seq, read before the page, when the page reads
to its end; else (`beforeSeq`, or `hasMore`) the page's own last record.

seenSeq.description: The cutover used by sinceSeen, null on a first visit. Absent from ordinary pages.

acpmux.FactKind.description: What a footer fact is about.

oneOf.description: The peer machine the session runs on (`text`); absent for this daemon's own.
Its folder (`text`, the whole path).
The branch its folder has checked out (`text`).
Its harness profile (`text`).
Its model (`text`).
How full its context is (`fraction`).
Its subagents that run now (`count`).
Its prompts that wait (`count`).
Its running turn (`since`, the turn's start).

acpmux.FooterFact.description: One piece of the footer's quiet metadata.

atRest.description:
Worth its words in the footer at rest, with no status and no hover: the machine of a
session on another machine, where a command does something else than here (RFD 0130: "a
chat on another machine earns its machine name in view"). The pane draws it only behind
its own switch (`composer-machine-at-rest`, default off). Absent otherwise.

fraction.description: The share of the context window used, 0 to 1.

live.description: Worth a counter in the footer row itself now; else the hover card lists it only.

since.description: The running turn's start, ms since the epoch.

acpmux.ForkParams.description:
`acp.session.fork`: a completed-turn, live, or before-prompt fork.
Before-prompt requests require requestId and omit both throughSeq and live.

beforePromptId.description: Recorded prompt identity, nonempty and at most 512 UTF-8 bytes. Claude/Codex only.

cancelToken.description:
The caller's name for this fork while it is made, at most 128 bytes: `_acpmux/kill` with
`cancelFork` and this token stops it, or takes it back once made (`hub/fork_cancel.rs`).

harness.description: With `live`: the harness the fork runs on, carrying the conversation over (a model switch).

mode.description:
With `live`: the permission mode the fork starts in, one of the modes the chat's harness
lists (`modes.availableModes`); another is refused. Capability `acp.session.fork.subagent.v1`.

model.description:
The model the fork starts on, at most 256 bytes: with `harness` that harness's, else the
chat's own harness's (set before the reply, or the fork is refused and removed).

requestId.description: Persisted retry identity, nonempty and at most 512 UTF-8 bytes; scoped to the source.

subagentId.description:
With `live`: fork one of the chat's subagents into a chat of its own, from the subagent's
own conversation, not the chat's (`hub/fork_subagent.rs`). The id `_meta.acpmux.subagents`
names it by, or its `agentId` (a Claude agent's id; a Codex child's thread id is its id).
A Claude Code or Codex chat only; a running subagent forks through its last settled step.
Capability `acp.session.fork.subagent.v1`.

acpmux.GoneRow.description: A row that left the list since a follow's cursor.

peer.description: The peer a remote session ran on.

acpmux.Lane.description: The session's lane (cx-v9k2f), decided once by the daemon (`views::lane`).

error.description: The failed or lost turn's error text, secrets masked (`secret_scan`).

since.description: Unix ms the state began; null when the daemon does not know.

stalledSince.description:
A `working` lane that has stalled: since when its turn has had no tool
call in flight and no sign of its model (`turn.stalledSince`); null
otherwise. The state stays `working`, so a client that reads only it
is unchanged.

step.description:
What the session is doing now, one line: the running turn's prompt,
else the agent's last reply line, secrets masked (`secret_scan`).

title.description:
The session's title, else its latest prompt, one line, secrets masked
(`secret_scan`).

acpmux.LastReturn.description:
A person's return to a chat that kept working (`hub/seen.rs`): the log seq they had seen when
they left, and how many turns ended while nobody showed it.

acpmux.LastTurn.description:
The outcome of the session's last turn. Keys the turn result lacked
are absent.

detail.description: Why a turn ended without an answer, e.g. `outcome_unknown`.

errorKind.description:
What kind of failure a failed turn was (`recovery.rs`): `disk.full`, `disk.low`,
`peer.unreachable`, `daemon.restarting`, `spawn.failed`, `agent.exited`,
`auth.signed_out` or `auth.expired`. A client treats a kind it does not know as a plain
error. The same key is on a request's error `data` and on the `turn_error` and
`turn_result` records.

heldUntil.description: When a `capacity` turn's continuation runs, while it waits.

recovery.description: One sentence saying what to do about the failure.

status.description:
`completed`, `failed` or `cancelled`; on a session row, `capacity` for a failed turn a
capacity error cut whose continuation acpmux waits for or runs (`hub/auto_resume.rs`).

acpmux.LifecycleReceipt.description:
A durable lifecycle fact supplied by an explicit producer. This contract
is intentionally optional and opaque to the session sidebar until a
producer wires it to a real controller receipt.

acpmux.LoopEpisodeSummary.description:
The bounded diagnosis shown beside a looping chat. The daemon emits one event when this
becomes active and another when progress clears it; the summary lets a newly attached client
render the current state without replaying the transcript.

acpmux.McpServerStatus.description: `failed` also for one that waits on a sign-in (Claude Code `needs-auth`).

acpmux.McpServerSummary.description: One MCP server a harness loaded (`SessionSummary::mcp_servers`).

acpmux.MemberApproverDecision.description: One group member's signed one-time allow: the member prompt's nonce and the signature.

acpmux.Participant.description:
One person in a chat. The hub never marks the caller's own entry: a connection may carry
several people, so the client compares ids (a caller with no author is `owner`).

devices.description: How many connections carry this person in the chat.

acpmux.PermissionGroup.description: A batch of permission requests from one turn, decided together.

decision.description: The decision taken, once one was.

decisions.description:
What a respond may choose: all three, or `deny` alone when a pending
item has no single allow-once option.

command.description:
A shell call's command as the agent wrote it, without the line acpmux put before a
subagent's command to name its caller (`bg_hook::without_subagent_mark`).

summary.description:
What the call does, in the agent's plain words (a shell call's `description`), for the
row in place of the command (Leo 2026-11-23: "i also dont know why you asked me this").

allowRefused.description:
Set when this reader's group allows would be refused, with the
refusal's reason (`permission.person_required`: only the person
allows a group, and a peer's link never is one). A deny still counts.

macAllowOnce.description:
Set (true) beside `allowRefused` when this daemon still counts a group's
one-time allow signed by an enrolled Mac for every pending member
(`_meta.acpmux.approverDecisions`, `hub/mac_approvers.rs`).

groupId.description: One group; absent lists them all. Never null.

acpmux.PermissionPending.description:
To attached clients (and watchers not attached) when a permission or
question waits: the log record's message (the agent's request with
acpmux's `permissionId`) plus where it came from.

decisionNonce.description: Signs an allow relayed for the person (`hub/person.rs`).

groupId.description: The batch it joined, if any.

annotations.description: Claude Code AskUserQuestion annotations beside the answers, by question text: `{preview?, notes?}`.

forkCheckpoint.description: Fork first (fork_risky.rs): the copy the app made before allowing, `{machine, fork, forkMs}`.

optionId.description: The option chosen; absent cancels the request.

acpmux.PersonHold.description:
What a daemon start holds for a person (`SessionSummary::person_hold`): the chat's folder and
why an agent does not start there unasked.

acpmux.PresenceNote.description:
`_acpmux/presence`, to every connection attached to the chat on each change, and
`presence` in the `_acpmux/attach` reply. Never in the log, `_acpmux/events` or an export.

participants.description: One per person, by id; at most 32 besides the owner.

acpmux.PromptClass.description: What another agent's message asks of the session it goes to.

oneOf.description: The sender cannot go on until the receiver acts.
The sender asks something and waits for the answer.
The sender reports work it finished. A message sent with no class is one.
Information to read at leisure.

acpmux.PurgedSession.description: A purged session: only its id is left.

acpmux.QueueOrigin.description: Who put a queued prompt in the queue ([`of`]).

oneOf.description: The person typed it: the composer's steer rows.
Another agent's message, or acpmux's notice or digest of such messages.
acpmux's own prompt to the chat's agent: no steer row and none of the person's actions.

acpmux.QueuedAuthor.description: The person who queued a prompt in a shared chat.

avatar.description:
Their profile picture (`_meta.provenance` `fromAvatar`, an `https://` URL), left out when
they have none (and from an older acpmux).

acpmux.QueuedImage.description: An image a queued prompt sends.

id.description:
The SHA-256 of its bytes (64 lowercase hex digits): `_acpmux/attachment {sessionId, id}`
reads it, and `_acpmux/queue_edit` `update` `images` keeps it.

name.description: Its file name, when the client gave one.

source.description: The app it came from (`{name, bundleId?, site?}`), as the prompt's display metadata named it. Absent otherwise.

acpmux.QueuedPromptSummary.description: A prompt waiting for the running turn to end.

author.description:
The teammate who queued it in a shared chat (`_meta.provenance` `person_message`,
`author.rs`), null for the owner's and for an agent's message: an app shows it under their
name and offers none of its own actions on it (only they change it, `queue.not_author`).
Kept across a restart and by their own edit.

awaitingOwner.description:
A person's prompt that waits for the chat's owner (`author.approval: "owner"`): the queue
runs past it until the owner approves it (`_acpmux/queue_approve`, naming `turnId` and `revision`) or
declines it (`_acpmux/queue_decline`). The owner's pane draws Approve and Decline on it.

class.description:
What another agent's message asks of this chat (`_meta.acpmux.class`, `prompt_class.rs`):
`result` when it named none; null for the person's own prompt and from a peer on an older
acpmux.

fromAgent.description:
The sending agent's name when it is another agent's message, null for the person's: an
app draws it as a received message waiting for the turn, not as a composer row.

fromHarness.description:
That session's harness family (`claude`, `codex`, ...), bound the same way: what an app
draws the sender's icon from. Null when unknown (a mesh relay carries none yet).

fromSessionId.description:
The sending session's id when the daemon bound it (its caller token, a peer daemon's word
on its own proven caller, the mesh relay's sender, a lane's report), null otherwise
(`prompt_provenance.rs` `FROM_SESSION_ID`). Display only, never authority.

held.description: Waits behind a failed turn until the queue is resumed.

heldByStop.description:
Another agent's message the person's Stop holds (`hub/cancel.rs`): it waits until the
person's next turn completes or the queue is resumed. False otherwise; absent from a peer
on an older acpmux.

images.description: The images it sends, in its order; `_acpmux/attachment` reads each by its id.

inboxNotice.description:
acpmux's inbox notice of other agents' messages (`_meta.provenance` `inbox_notice`,
`hub/inbox.rs`): that provenance, `{kind, noticeId, threads}`, so an app draws it as the
messages it carries and never as the person's queued prompt, also when it has not read
its `queued` record (a chat reopened on a recent page). Null for any other prompt, and
once edited (an edit drops the provenance).

origin.description:
Who put it in the queue, from its provenance alone (`hub/queue_origin.rs`): `person` (the
composer's steer rows), `agent` (another agent's message or acpmux's notice of such), or
`acpmux` (the daemon's own prompt: a surge digest, a subagent's resume, a cut turn's
continuation), which an app draws apart from the person's rows with none of their actions.
Absent from an older acpmux.

provenance.description:
Its `_meta.provenance` when it names a sender that is no agent's to act on: another agent's
message the person edited (`editedBy`, still that agent's words to read) or a prompt no
proof attributes (`unverified`). An app draws its card from it while `fromAgent` is null.
Null otherwise. Display only, never authority.

revision.description: Its version for the owner's approval: 0 when queued, one more at each edit by its author.

subagentRetry.description:
acpmux's own ask that the chat's agent resume a subagent that failed on a transient error
(`_meta.provenance` `subagent_retry`, `hub/subagent_retry.rs`): an app draws it as that
subagent's resume, not as the person's prompt. Null for any other prompt, and once edited
(an edit drops the provenance).

acpmux.QueuedSubagentRetry.description: The subagent a queued resume asks the agent to resume (`QueuedPromptSummary.subagentRetry`).

agentId.description: The Agent tool's id for it, which the agent resumes it by.

error.description: The transient error it failed on.

name.description: Its task or name, when acpmux knew one.

cmuxGesture.description:
The app's gesture ticket for this exact pick (`transport.gesture`);
the app's relay reads it, acpmux does not.

acpmux.RetryKind.description: What `_acpmux/retry` retried: the chat's own turn, or one of its subagents.

acpmux.RetryParams.description:
`_acpmux/retry` (the Retry button, `acpmux retry`): retry the chat's failed last turn now,
in the same session (`hub/auto_resume/retry_turn.rs`).

sessionId.description: The chat's id, name or unique prefix.

subagentId.description:
One of the chat's failed subagents to resume instead, by its id or agent id
(`hub/subagent_retry_manual.rs`), never taken as the chat's own turn.

acpmux.RetryReason.description:
Why a turn is retried (`hub::turn_errors::resume_cause`): the provider or the gateway had no
capacity (HTTP 503 or 529, overloaded, no account free), the account hit its usage or rate
limit (`rate_limit`, HTTP 429: the chat holds every turn until the reset, `hub/rate_hold.rs`),
the connection dropped, the agent process died mid-turn, the chat outgrew its model's
context window (`context`: it is compacted, then continued at once), or the machine's disk
was full (`disk`: it goes on once space is free again).

acpmux.RetryResult.description:
What `_acpmux/retry` sent: the prompt `promptId` (for the chat's turn `P~resume-n`, the next
attempt of the failed prompt; for a subagent `subagent-retry-<tool>-<attempt>-<ms>`) and the turn
it started.

acpmux.RetrySummary.description:
An automatic retry of a failed turn that waits (`hub/auto_resume.rs`): attempt `attempt`
of `of`, at `nextAt` (epoch ms). It sends the prompt `promptId~resume-<attempt>` in the same
session, for the cut turn `turnId`.

acpmux.SessionChanged.description:
To watchers when a session changed: its new summary (only its id when
purged), the coarse `kind` and the log record behind it.

listSeq.description:
The list position this change took (`hub/row_log.rs`): the client's cursor for
`_acpmux/watch {afterSeq}` is the highest it applied.

peer.description: The peer a remote session runs on.

rowSeq.description:
To a connection that asked for patches (`initialize` `_meta.acpmux.sessionChangedDelta`):
this row's number among the chat's rows it heard; the next `_acpmux/session_patch` of the
chat applies to it (`server/session_patch.rs`). Absent for every other connection.

acpmux.SessionDetail.description:
A session as `_acpmux/attach` returns it: its summary plus what an
attached client draws (`Hub::session_detail`).

approvedPlan.description:
The plan the person last approved in this chat (`hub/plan_build.rs`), which the pane keeps
in sight while the agent builds it. Absent until one, and from a peer on an older acpmux.

backgroundsWork.description:
`_acpmux/process/background` (Ctrl-B) moves its foreground work: its
harness is Claude Code (claude-stdio), whatever the harness's name.
Clients offer Ctrl-B from this, not from `harness`.

capacityWait.description:
It waits for capacity and goes on by itself (`hub/capacity_wait.rs`). Absent otherwise,
and from a peer on an older acpmux.

children.description: Its sub-sessions that are not closed.

composerStatus.description:
The composer footer's status dot and quiet metadata, decided from this row's own fields
(`protocol/composer_status.rs`); set on the row after it is built, and again by this
daemon on a peer's row (with `peer`). Whole on a read with tools (attach, info, the
attached chat's `session_changed`); a census row carries it only with an item or a live
fact, and without the facts that repeat its own fields (`composer_status::census`).
Absent from an older acpmux.

createdBy.description:
Who created it (`hub/created_by.rs`): `{kind: "person"|"agent"|"script", workspace?,
session?}`, decided by the daemon from the connection, never from a request value.
Null for a fork, a moved-in session and one saved before it existed; absent from a
peer on an older acpmux.

credentialOnlyHere.description:
It holds its owner's launch credential (`agent_credentials.rs`) while its agent is
hibernated, so the credential is in this daemon's memory and nowhere else: a daemon restart
now loses it, and the chat's next start runs without it. `acpmux session wake` starts the
agent, whose env then carries the credential across the restart; a machine update does that
before it restarts this daemon. Says only that one is held, never its name or value. Absent
otherwise, and from an older acpmux.

cwd.description: Lossy when the path is not UTF-8.

depth.description:
Its lineage depth (`parent`): 0 for a root session, 1 for the sessions
its agent started, and so on.

displayName.description:
The name every human-visible surface shows for it (tab, sidebar row, lists, chat header,
notices, a message's sender): its handle when one was given (`acpmux rename @ Mango
--handle`), absent otherwise (a derived handle is no name a person chose; show `name`).
Its former names and handles are `formerNames` ("Mango (fka claude-sr2-coord-old)").

effort.description:
The harness's current reasoning effort, when it reports one.
Additive for older clients and peers.

forkSeq.description: Where a fork branched off its parent.

forksAnyTurn.description:
Whether the chat forks, and edits, through any completed turn, not only its latest: its
harness cuts a conversation at a turn (Claude Code and Codex, `config::turn_cut`), whatever
family name its profile carries. Absent when unknown (the configuration was being written
as the summary was built) and from a peer on an older acpmux: a client then falls back to
the family, never reads absence as false.

formerNames.description:
The names it had before its renames, oldest first: each still names it where no session
has it as its current name. Absent when it was never renamed, and from an older acpmux.

handle.description: The session's spoken handle, independent of its task name and ids. Older peers omit it.

harnessSandboxError.description: The refused operation, redacted and bounded; cleared on recovery.

harnessSandboxFailed.description:
Unix milliseconds when its harness first refused a command because the harness's own
sandbox did not start (`hub/harness_sandbox.rs`). Omitted for peers.

harnessSandboxFailing.description:
Whether its harness refuses commands now for that reason; a completed command or a new
harness process ends it (`hub/harness_sandbox.rs`). Omitted for peers.

hasDraft.description:
Its composer holds typed text not sent yet (`composerDraft`, non-blank): an app update
that installs when idle (`updates.installWhenIdle`) waits for it. Absent otherwise, and from
a peer on an older acpmux.

icon.description:
The icon it set (`session_icon.rs`), drawn like a harness `iconSpec`; absent draws the
harness mark.

indicator.description: The status dot every client draws (`status_indicator`); null for none.

inputSince.description: Since when it waits on the person (`lane`); null while it does not.

lane.description: What it is doing and since when (`views::lane`); null for a closed session.

lastMessage.description: One sidebar line; null before the first prompt.

lastReturn.description:
The person's return to the chat while they stay on it (`hub/seen.rs`): `since` and the
`turns` that ended unseen. A client opening the chat then draws "New since you looked" at
`since`, also when its attach answers before its list read.

lifecycleReceipt.description:
An optional controller/daemon lifecycle receipt. It is absent until a
producer supplies a validated receipt; clients must not infer one from
status or placement fields.

loopEpisode.description:
A live repeated-tool episode (`hub/loop_detector.rs`), if this turn is looping.
Additive so older clients and peers can omit it.

mcpServers.description:
The MCP servers the harness says it loaded, from its own report (Claude
Code's system/init); null when it reports none (every ACP harness).

movedTo.description:
Moved to another daemon (`acpmux session move`): where it runs now,
`{host?, sessionId, cwd?, branch?, commit?}`. It never runs here again. Absent otherwise,
and from a peer on an older acpmux.

moving.description: Being moved to another daemon; it takes no prompt meanwhile.

nameGiven.description:
Someone gave `name` (at the start, a fork's or a rename), not the daemon's `HARNESS-N`
default. Absent otherwise, from a session named before it was kept, and from a peer on an
older acpmux.

parent.description:
The session whose agent started this one (`acpmux new` in its shell, or its
`start_session` tool), recorded at creation from the proven caller; null for a
session a person or the app started. Not the fork parent (`parentId`). Absent
from a peer on an older acpmux.

peer.description: The peer daemon a remote session runs on; absent for this daemon's own.

pending.description: Permission requests waiting for an answer.

personHold.description:
A daemon start holds what this chat queued until a person opens it: its folder is guarded
(`hub/protected_hold.rs`). `session resume` names it and NOW says why the queue does not
drain. Absent otherwise, and from a peer on an older acpmux.

pinned.description:
A person pinned it (`_acpmux/pin`), on any of their replicas (`hub/synced.rs`). Absent
otherwise, and from a peer on an older acpmux.

pullRequests.description:
The pull request URLs its `gh pr create` calls printed, oldest first;
absent from a peer on an older acpmux.

queuePaused.description: A turn failed: the prompts behind it wait for a client to resume them.

rateLimitParked.description:
Since when (Unix ms) this chat is parked on the rate limit: six turns in a row failed on
it, or Stop came while the limit had it, so it starts nothing by itself until `acpmux
retry` or the person's own prompt (`hub/rate_hold.rs`). Absent otherwise, and from a peer
on an older acpmux.

rateLimitedUntil.description:
The account's rate limit holds every turn of this chat until this time (Unix ms): what
comes in queues and goes in as one turn at the reset (`hub/rate_hold.rs`). `acpmux ls` shows
"rate-limited until HH:MMZ". Absent otherwise, and from a peer on an older acpmux.

retiredAgentSessionIds.description:
The chat's earlier native ids, oldest first (`SessionMeta::retired_agent_session_ids`):
a Codex chat's earlier roots, which its older records still name, so a client folding
them never reads one as a subagent. Absent when none, and from a peer on an older acpmux.

retry.description:
The automatic retry of its failed last turn that waits (`hub/auto_resume.rs`); null
when none waits.

retryDeciding.description:
Its last turn failed on an error an automatic retry answers, and whether, and when, it
is retried is not settled yet: `retry` is about to be set or stay null, or the retry is
starting or runs (`hub/auto_resume.rs`). `_acpmux/wait` answers for that turn once it is
settled. Absent otherwise, and from a peer on an older acpmux.

root.description:
The root of its lineage tree: the first ancestor no agent started; its own
id for a root. Absent from a peer on an older acpmux.

rules.description: The session has its own permission rules.

seenSeq.description:
The log seq the person had seen when they last stopped showing the chat: a client
opening it while `unreadTurns` is above 0 draws "New since you looked" after it.

shortName.description: Its name among its parent's sub-sessions; null for a root.

shown.description: Some attached client shows the chat.

spawnToolCallId.description: The parent's tool call that started it, when acpmux could tell.

spawnedBy.description:
The session whose agent started this one, kept only while that parent
is listed and is a root itself: one level, for lists that fold one level.
`parent` without those rules, else an older client's `spawnedBy` tag.

startedBy.description:
The session whose agent started this one with its `start_session`
tool (`hub/subsessions.rs`); null for a session a person or client
started. Kept when the parent is closed or gone, so a client draws
the tree from these links at any depth.

starting.description:
Its agent is being started (a start, a wake or a mode change holds the session's spawn
lease, as `stop --if-idle` reads it): a daemon restart now ends that start, so an update
waits on it as on a turn. Always sent, so a row without it is from an older acpmux,
which an update reads by its row's age instead.

state.description: Effective liveness: `stopping` while a Stop waits for its turn to end, `stuck` after three classified harness failures, else `status`.

steering.description: The agent takes a prompt mid-turn.

stuckError.description: Last classified error, redacted and bounded. Omitted for peers.

stuckSince.description: Unix milliseconds when the third failure established stuck. Omitted for peers.

timeBreakdown.description:
Incremental wall-time and token attribution for the chat. This is seeded by a detail or
attach read and omitted from census rows until then (`hub/time_breakdown.rs`).

titleSource.description:
Who supplied `title`: `prompt` is the first-prompt fallback, while
`harness`, `generated` and `adopted` are real chat titles. Older peers
may omit this field.

tools.description: The chat's tools (`hub/tools.rs`), present on per-session reads and attachments.

toolsMutable.description: `_acpmux/set_tools` can change them; omitted from census rows.

transcriptSeq.description:
The seq of its newest transcript record (`hub/paging.rs` `is_transcript`): unlike
`updatedAt` and `lastSeq`, bookkeeping (an agent start's `agent_start_waiting`, usage,
git, process counts) never moves it, so a client that keeps a chat's newest page reads it
again only when this passes the value it read at. An upper bound after a hard stop.
Absent from a peer on an older acpmux.

unreadTurns.description:
Turns that ended while no client showed the chat, since a person last showed it
(`hub/seen.rs`): the sidebar's count. Absent from a peer on an older acpmux.

usageStats.description:
What its harness spends and holds, from the harness's own records
(`usage_stats.rs`); absent until a Claude Code or Codex chat's records
are found, for any other harness, and from a peer on an older acpmux.

waitingOn.description:
What it waits on the person for: `question` (an agent question), `permission`,
`secret` (a private card asking a secret's value), `elevation` (a card asking the
password to run one command as root) or `mcp_connect` (a card asking to connect an MCP
server); null while it waits on nothing. A `waiting` status always has one. Only the
person allows a permission or answers a card.

waitingPrompt.description: The first prompt of the question it waits on, cut to 120 characters.

waitsForSlot.description:
A sub-session whose queued prompt waits for a free run slot of its parent: the parent
runs as many sub-sessions as its `maxRunning` allows (`hub/subsession_runs.rs`). Absent
otherwise, and from a peer on an older acpmux.

watching.description: The family of a conversation another app runs that this chat only shows; null otherwise.

workingBelow.description:
Work runs below it with no turn open: a background subagent, a harness background process,
or a sub-session at work (what keeps the idle pass from ending it, `hub/idle.rs`). An app
update that installs when idle waits for it. Absent otherwise, and from a peer on an older
acpmux.

acpmux.SessionEvent.description: One record of a session's log (`server::event_value`).

dir.description:
`in` (agent to acpmux), `out` (acpmux to agent), `mux` (acpmux's own)
or `peer`.

kind.description:
The JSON-RPC method, the `sessionUpdate` value, or an acpmux kind such
as `status`.

msg.description: The raw JSON-RPC message, or acpmux's payload.

acpmux.SessionIcon.description: The icon clients draw for one chat.

oneOf.description: An agent mark id from design/agent-icons (`claude`, `gemini`, ...).
One emoji.
An SF Symbol; `text` and `hue` are the monogram a client that cannot draw it shows.
An SVG, PNG, ICO or JPEG, base64, so a page draws it with no file or network access.

acpmux.SessionPatch.description:
To a connection that asked for patches (`initialize` `_meta.acpmux.sessionChangedDelta`), in
place of a `_acpmux/session_changed` once it holds the chat's row: only what changed
(`server/session_patch.rs`). `patch` is a JSON merge patch (RFC 7386; `null` removes a key)
of the row it holds at `baseRowSeq`, in which `{"$splice": [from, keep, items]}` stands for
an array that is `held[from..from + keep]` then `items`; the result is the row at `rowSeq`.

peer.description: The peer a remote session runs on.

qualifiedSessionId.description: A peer's chat: the id its row has here.

acpmux.SessionSummary.description:
One session as every list shows it (`Hub::session_summary`). A peer's
session arrives as the peer daemon's own summary plus `peer`, with
`status` `unreachable` while the peer is gone; a peer on an older
acpmux may lack newer fields, so nullable ones are optional here.

approvedPlan.description:
The plan the person last approved in this chat (`hub/plan_build.rs`), which the pane keeps
in sight while the agent builds it. Absent until one, and from a peer on an older acpmux.

backgroundsWork.description:
`_acpmux/process/background` (Ctrl-B) moves its foreground work: its
harness is Claude Code (claude-stdio), whatever the harness's name.

children.description: Its sub-sessions that are not closed.

starting.description:
Its agent is being started (a start, a wake or a mode change holds the session's spawn
lease, as `stop --if-idle` reads it): a daemon restart now ends that start, so an update
waits on it as on a turn. Always sent, so a row without it is from an older acpmux,
which an update reads by its row's age instead.

state.description: Effective liveness: `stopping` while a Stop waits for its turn to end, `stuck` after three classified harness failures, else `status`.

steering.description: The agent takes a prompt mid-turn.

stuckError.description: Last classified error, redacted and bounded. Omitted for peers.

stuckSince.description: Unix milliseconds when the third failure established stuck. Omitted for peers.

timeBreakdown.description:
Incremental wall-time and token attribution for the chat. This is seeded by a detail or
attach read and omitted from census rows until then (`hub/time_breakdown.rs`).

titleSource.description:
Who supplied `title`: `prompt` is the first-prompt fallback, while
`harness`, `generated` and `adopted` are real chat titles. Older peers
may omit this field.

tools.description: The chat's tools (`hub/tools.rs`), present on per-session reads and attachments.

toolsMutable.description: `_acpmux/set_tools` can change them; omitted from census rows.

transcriptSeq.description:
The seq of its newest transcript record (`hub/paging.rs` `is_transcript`): unlike
`updatedAt` and `lastSeq`, bookkeeping (an agent start's `agent_start_waiting`, usage,
git, process counts) never moves it, so a client that keeps a chat's newest page reads it
again only when this passes the value it read at. An upper bound after a hard stop.
Absent from a peer on an older acpmux.

unreadTurns.description:
Turns that ended while no client showed the chat, since a person last showed it
(`hub/seen.rs`): the sidebar's count. Absent from a peer on an older acpmux.

usageStats.description:
What its harness spends and holds, from the harness's own records
(`usage_stats.rs`); absent until a Claude Code or Codex chat's records
are found, for any other harness, and from a peer on an older acpmux.

waitingOn.description:
What it waits on the person for: `question` (an agent question), `permission`,
`secret` (a private card asking a secret's value), `elevation` (a card asking the
password to run one command as root) or `mcp_connect` (a card asking to connect an MCP
server); null while it waits on nothing. A `waiting` status always has one. Only the
person allows a permission or answers a card.

waitingPrompt.description: The first prompt of the question it waits on, cut to 120 characters.

waitsForSlot.description:
A sub-session whose queued prompt waits for a free run slot of its parent: the parent
runs as many sub-sessions as its `maxRunning` allows (`hub/subsession_runs.rs`). Absent
otherwise, and from a peer on an older acpmux.

watching.description: The family of a conversation another app runs that this chat only shows; null otherwise.

workingBelow.description:
Work runs below it with no turn open: a background subagent, a harness background process,
or a sub-session at work (what keeps the idle pass from ending it, `hub/idle.rs`). An app
update that installs when idle waits for it. Absent otherwise, and from a peer on an older
acpmux.

cursor.description: A previous reply's `nextCursor`: the page starts after that session.

excludeStatus.description: `_acpmux/sessions` only: exclude these statuses before pagination.

limit.description: Page size, at least 1. Without it the reply is the whole list.

localOnly.description: `_acpmux/sessions` only: exclude peer sessions before pagination.

orderBy.description: `_acpmux/sessions` only: `sessionId` orders by immutable ID for complete scans.

peer.description:
`_acpmux/sessions` only (a watch refuses it): only the sessions this acpmux peer owns
(its name, e.g. `huge-blue`). Empty is no filter.

pendingOnly.description:
`_acpmux/sessions` only (a watch refuses it): only the sessions with a pending permission
or question, local and peer, summarized alone and answered without the list's pace.
Takes no other filter; the reply is never paged (capability `session-list-pending-v1`).

status.description:
`_acpmux/sessions` only (a watch refuses it): only the sessions in this status
(`running`, `ready`, `idle`, `waiting`, `closed`). Empty is no filter.

topLevelOnly.description:
`_acpmux/sessions` only (a watch refuses it): exclude side chats (a `side` tag) and
sessions another chat's agent started (`spawnedBy`, `startedBy`) before pagination: the
chats a list shows on their own (capability `session-list-top-level-v1`).

usage.description:
`_acpmux/sessions` only: read each chat's usage from its harness's records first
(`usageStats`; at most one read every 5 s, waited for at most 750 ms). Without it the
rows carry what the last read found.

withTools.description: Include tool inventories explicitly; default census rows omit them.

follow.description:
A watch that sent `afterSeq`: `sessions` holds only the rows changed since, and `gone` the
rows that went; the client's other rows stand.

gone.description: With `follow`: the rows that went since `afterSeq`.

listEpoch.description: With `listSeq`: this daemon run's id for list positions.

listSeq.description:
A watch's reply: the list position it is current to (`hub/row_log.rs`). Every change after
it reaches the watcher as a `session_changed` with a higher `listSeq`; a row replaces the
one held only when its position is not lower.

more.description:
With `follow`: cut at the page's size; `listSeq` is the last position it holds, and the
client follows again from there.

nextCursor.description:
With `limit`: the cursor for the next page, null when the list is
done. Absent without `limit`.

reset.description:
A watch whose `afterSeq` the log could not follow (another daemon run, or older than its
oldest removal): this is the list's first page, and the client drops the rows it held.

sessions.description: Local and peer sessions, newest first, then by `sessionId`.

acpmux.StatusAction.description: The one thing a person does about an item.

oneOf.description: Dial the machine again now (`_acpmux/peer_reconnect`).
Resume the prompts a failed turn paused.
Sign in again.
Update the machine.

acpmux.StatusItem.description: One entry of the dot's rundown.

action.description: The one thing a person does about it; absent when there is none.

showAt.description: The dot shows it no earlier than this, ms since the epoch; absent: at once.

since.description: Since when it holds, ms since the epoch; absent when unknown.

subject.description: The machine or harness the words name as `{subject}`; absent when they name none.

until.description: When it ends on its own (a rate limit's reset), ms since the epoch; absent otherwise.

acpmux.StatusKind.description: What an item is about. One words-key prefix each ([`StatusKind::words_prefix`]).

oneOf.description: The link to the machine a peer session runs on (`_acpmux/peer_state_changed` `status`).
The account's rate limit holds the chat's turns (`rateLimitedUntil`, `rateLimitParked`).
Its harness failed three times in a row (`stuckReason`).
A turn failed and the prompts behind it wait to be resumed (`queuePaused`).

Its harness refuses commands because its own sandbox did not start
(`harnessSandboxFailing`).
Pane-local, never sent by acpmux: the pane's link to its agent service.
Pane-local, never sent by acpmux: the pane restores its sessions.
Pane-local, never sent by acpmux: the pane holds sends it could not deliver yet.

acpmux.StatusLevel.description: How much an item matters; ordered, `problem` worst.

oneOf.description: Worth a glance; it heals on its own.
Something waits on time or on a person, and nothing is broken.
Broken until a person acts.

promptId.description:
The prompt the turn answers (its record's `promptId`): a chat on the row store names a turn
by its prompt, not by `turnId`. None for a turn whose records carry no `promptId`.

turnTokens.description: Whole-turn usage, not usage attributed to this interval.

acpmux.ToolSummary.description: One row of a chat's tool list (`store::ToolRow`).

canToggle.description: `_acpmux/set_tools` can turn it on or off in this chat.

source.description: What gives it: `cmux`, or the harness that reported it (`claude`).

activity.description:
What the turn does right now: its latest tool call's title, masked
(`secret_scan`); null until it calls one (`hub/activity.rs`).

acpmux.UsageStats.description:
A chat's spend and context as its harness recorded them (`usage_stats.rs`):
Claude Code's transcript and its subagents' (their spend is the chat's), or
Codex's rollout. Read from where the last read ended: by a session list
that asks (`usage: true`) or an info read, at most every 5 s, and by each
turn's end for its own chat, recorded then as a mux `usage_stats` record.
A value that could not be read is null, never 0: a count is null while
the reads have not covered the whole last day (a first read cut short
before it, a backlog not read yet, a file that could not be read).

autocompact.description: Whether something caps the context at which the harness compacts.

autocompactCap.description:
The cap, when `autocompact` is `capped` and its value is known (Claude
Code's `--autocompact`, `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW`,
`CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE` of a known window, `autoCompactWindow`;
Codex's `model_auto_compact_token_limit`); null otherwise.

cacheReadByModel1h.description: Cache-read prompt tokens by call model in the rolling last hour.

cacheReadByModelPreviousUtcHour.description: Cache-read prompt tokens by call model in the completed UTC hour preceding updatedAt.

cacheReadShare24h.description:
Of those calls' prompt tokens (input, cache read and cache write), the share the prompt
cache served (0 to 1); null with no calls or when the day is not read whole.

calls24h.description: Model calls of the last 24 hours, subagents' included.

contextTokens.description: The last call's context: its input, cache read and cache write tokens.

contextWindow.description: The model's context window, as the harness reported it, else the catalog's.

costPerCallUsd24h.description: `costUsd24h` over the priced calls: what one call costs at list prices, USD.

costUsd24h.description:
Those tokens at the model catalog's list prices, USD; null when no model
they ran on has a price, or when `tokens24h` is null.

launcher.description:
The executable its harness runs, by file name (`claude`, `claude-sr2`,
`codex-acp`); `harness` is the profile. Null when this daemon did not
start it (an adopted, watched or revived chat).

subagents1h.description: Subagents started in the last hour.

subagents24h.description: Subagents started in the last 24 hours.

tokens24h.description:
Tokens of the last 24 hours, subagents' included: input, output, cache
read and cache write.

tokensByModelPreviousUtcHour.description: Tokens per call model in the completed UTC hour preceding the hour of updatedAt.

updatedAt.description: Unix ms of the read these come from.

afterSeq.description:
Follow the list from this position (`hub/row_log.rs`, capability
`session-list-follow-v1`): the highest `listSeq` the client applied. The reply holds the
rows changed since and `gone`, not the list (`follow: true`); one the log cannot follow is
answered with the list's first page and `reset: true`.

enabled.description:
Default true: every session's changes arrive as
`_acpmux/session_changed`.

listEpoch.description: The `listEpoch` that `afterSeq` came with: a cursor of another daemon run is reset.

withTools.description: Include tool inventories explicitly; default census rows omit them.

mac_participants.description: Size-state participant ids of the surface's terminal that are this host's own views; empty without surface.

order.description: Device tokens, highest first: mac (this host's own views) or device:<id>; at most 32.
Device tokens, highest first: mac or device:<id> (1 to 128 of [A-Za-z0-9_.:-]); at most 32. Omitted keeps the stored order.

done.description: Units of the phase done (agent_roster: journal rows folded); null when the phase does not count.

elapsed_ms.description: Milliseconds since the owner bound its socket and began the restore.

last_advance_ms.description: When the restore last advanced (a new phase or a new done count), in milliseconds since it began.

phase.description: The restore step running now: registry_open, schema, migrations, integrity, snapshot, agent_roster, mux_build, browsers, host_adoption, reconcile or finish. Clients show an unknown name as is.

total.description: Units of the phase in all; null when unknown.

api_revision.description: The API revision this daemon reads and writes natively (cmux-tui/spec/api-compat.json). Absent on daemons from before revisions. Only with identify {revisions: true}.

api_version.description: The newest dated API version this daemon serves (YYYY-MM-DD; cmux-tui/spec/api-versioning.md). Only with identify {revisions: true}.

build_time.description: Unix seconds of the source commit this daemon was built from; null when unknown. A client that updates the machine compares it with its own to never move the machine back to an older build. Only with identify {revisions: true}.

crate_version.description: The cmux-tui crate version; `version` is the npm/PyPI release (equal in app and local builds). Only with identify {revisions: true}.

install.description: How this daemon's binary was installed: npm, pypi, app or other. Only with identify {revisions: true}.

min_api_revision.description: The oldest API revision this daemon translates to and from for a client that declares it with set-client-info. Only with identify {revisions: true}.

min_api_version.description: The oldest dated API version this daemon still serves for a client that pins it with set-client-info api_version. Only with identify {revisions: true}.

restore.description: Only with identify {restore_progress: true}, and only while the owner restores its session (lifecycle_ready false): what the restore does now. A restore that advances moves last_advance_ms; one that hangs keeps it while elapsed_ms grows.

screen_device_id.description: The authenticated cmux Remote worker's independently generated screen UUID; present only with identify {machine_metadata: true}, and null when no worker screen identity is currently available.

update_command.description: The command that updates this daemon's install (npm and PyPI only), for a client's version-skew refusal. Only with identify {revisions: true}.

expanded.description: Must identify a member of panes.

tree_revision.description: Opaque; from the tree_revision of the last whole tree.

epoch.description: Opaque; the epoch of the last reply applied ("" when none).

seq.description: The seq of the last reply applied (0 when none).

api_revision.description: The numbered revision behind api_version. Only when the request sent api_version.

api_version.description: The dated API version that serves this connection (YYYY-MM-DD). Only when the request sent api_version.

fixed.description: Grid used by mode fixed; clamped to at least 2 x 1.

priority.description: Priority keys `<user_id or anon:id>/<device_kind>`, highest first.

device_id.description: Stable per-install device id; tells two devices of one user apart.

device_kind.description: mac, iphone, ipad, tui, browser, linux, windows; anything else is unknown.

user_id.description: Asserted by the client; the daemon does not verify it.

palette.description: Decimal string keys are palette indexes 0 through 255.

changed.description: With delta: every workspace entry that changed past the cursor, as the whole tree renders it; replace the entry with the same id, or add it.

delta.description: True when the reply answers since with only what changed: workspaces is then empty; apply changed and removed to the tree you hold.

epoch.description: Opaque, random per daemon run; only in replies to a request with since. Send it back in since.

next.description: With limit: the after of the next page, on every page that is not the last.

order.description: With delta, when the order of the workspaces changed: every id, in the tree's order.

removed.description: With delta: the ids of the workspaces no longer in the tree.

seq.description: Only in replies to a request with since. Send it back in since.

total.description: With limit: the number of workspaces in the session.

tree_revision.description: Opaque revision of everything the tree shows; only in replies to a request with known. Send it back in known.

unchanged.description: True when the request's known tree is current: workspaces is then empty, and the client keeps the tree it holds.
